summary: Operator site is a restaurant page whose only RV wording is 'convenient parking for semis, RVs, and buses'; no sites, hookups or rate published. The 6 electric sites, $20-30 rate and Harvest Hosts tie are known only from RV LIFE and camper reports. Nothing written; inclusion flagged for review.
flags: INCLUSION / DROP CANDIDATE (reviewer decides): the operator's own page presents this as restaurant parking, not a campground: 'Traveling through? We offer convenient parking for semis, RVs, and buses.' (2026-11-24; the January 2026 version said 'Come stay with us - wheather you're with harvest host or you just need a spot to park your RV overnight'). It publishes no RV sites, no hookups, no nightly rate and no booking route. The six electric sites (two with water) exist only in camper reports: RV LIFE lists 6 sites, 50-amp, with a 2026-02-07 photo of 'Electric site 6', and its review digest advises calling ahead to reserve hookups. RV LIFE's $$ tier (avg $23, high $30) supplies PRICE and the restaurant's website + phone + Google 4.4/2,793 supply PRESENCE, so it passes the ordinary private test on paper; whether hookup sites sold by the night at a restaurant, largely as a Harvest Hosts stop, are a campground is the open question.

PRICE: no operator-posted rate (the stored note's '$20/night' is from Harvest Hosts/Campendium). The operator has a web page, so a camper-reported rate cannot price the entry; fees left empty. RV LIFE's highest_rate $30 is far under the $50 gate.
LONG-STAY: nothing long-stay in character (no monthly, seasonal or resident wording anywhere); not 55+; no minimum stay stated. Google 4.4 (2,793 reviews) is the restaurant's.

Phone 423-351-7190 confirmed (operator page and Google); website unchanged. Pin fine (Google 35.5966,-84.4923, stored 35.5965,-84.4923). The Harvest Hosts listing needs a membership login and was not read; Facebook not read. Hookups/sites (derived) left as stored: the operator is silent and only an aggregator speaks to them.
